grand_strategy.reading: Brazil plays the strategy of a continental power that will not take sides. It sells soybeans and beef to China, trades with the EU, speaks for the Global South in the BRICS and wants to lead on the Amazon, while US tariffs and sanctions and Argentina's feud push it to lean on its own bloc. The 25 October runoff is the constraint that decides how long this holds, because the sovereignty line that works against Washington is also the line that the Bolsonaro camp contests. Brazil's partners are many and none is a bloc of its own, so its room is the room that the vote leaves.

stances.note: Brazil's side of a pair the US card reads as rival (USA stance toward BRA, same sources). Brasilia cooperates out of necessity - the US is the market that the 2025 tariff and the 2026 Section 301 duty target - and resists alignment: it condemned the US removal of Maduro in January 2026 as an 'unacceptable line'. Warming on the same facts as the USA card: the Moraes delisting of 12 Dec 2025 and the partial rollback of the tariff. Bond - grievance: the 50% tariff was imposed over the Bolsonaro trial, an open wound. No Brazilian official statement on the tariff itself is cited here; the grade is a reading, confidence C.

stances_toward.note: Rival, warming - a reading, not a label (confidence C). Washington used its heaviest economic tools on a democracy over a domestic trial: a 50% tariff by executive order (30 Jul 2025) calling the Bolsonaro case a 'witch hunt', Global Magnitsky sanctions on Justice de Moraes the same day, a Section 301 case ending in a 25% duty (15 Jul 2026), and the threat of tariffs on BRICS members; Brasilia answered with trade diversification and de-dollarisation talk. Competing interests and open friction, no will to destroy - rival rather than reluctant_partner, because Washington chose coercion over cooperation. Warming: the Moraes sanctions were lifted (12 Dec 2025), the Senate voted 52-48 against the tariffs, and Lula and Trump met in May 2026. Bond - none. Brazil has no card yet.
